method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the figure is a cone with its top cut off parallel to the base, so it can be viewed as a large cone minus a smaller similar cone. From the text, the frustum has bottom radius 8 cm, top radius 4 cm, and height 6 cm. Because radii in similar cones are proportional to heights from the apex, the missing small cone and the full cone have radii ratio 4:8=1:2, so their heights are also in ratio 1:2. The frustum height is the difference of these heights, so if the small cone height is x, the full cone height is 2x and 2x−x=6, giving x=6 and full cone height 12. Compute volume as full cone minus small cone: (1/3)π·8^2·12 − (1/3)π·4^2·6 = 256π − 32π = 224π, so n=224.
